result.rationale: The migration inserts old setting values verbatim via raw SQL INSERT, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization (host.sub! of scheme and path). The removed site_setting_spec explicitly tested that 'http://eviltrout.com' and 'https://example.com/1234' were valid setting entries, so such values exist in the wild. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host), so a stored 'http://eviltrout.com' will never match referer host 'eviltrout.com', silently breaking embedding after upgrade.

judged_text: The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim without applying the model's normalization (scheme/path stripping in EmbeddableHost's before_validation), so values like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'example.com/1234' — both of which the old setting supported per the removed site_setting_spec cases — are stored unnormalized. After upgrade, EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares uri.host against the stored string and never matches these rows, so sites whose old setting used scheme- or path-form entries silently lose embedding (comments/embed actions raise InvalidAccess) with no error surfaced to the admin.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, legacy site_settings 'embeddable_hosts' values are inserted verbatim (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without running EmbeddableHost's `before_validation` normalization that strips scheme and path. The previous SiteSetting logic/tests explicitly supported entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`, but the new runtime check `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the DB row contains `http://eviltrout.com` or a path, it will never equal `eviltrout.com`, causing `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to return false and embedding to break post-upgrade.
